internal_refs.relationship: FEHA §12940(h) retaliation and §1102.5 whistleblower often arise from same facts — both must be pursued concurrently; different SOLs
§132a WC retaliation and §1102.5 may overlap if WC claim disclosed employer violations — coordinate filing strategy

external_refs.relationship: If protected disclosure related to federal financial fraud (wire fraud, RICO) — federal anti-retaliation provisions (SOX §806, Dodd-Frank) may overlap with §1102.5
Internal communications showing employer's belief that employee would disclose are critical §1102.5(b) evidence — discoverable via CCP §2023 spoliation analysis if destroyed

case_law.citation: Patten v. Grant Joint Union High School Dist., 134 Cal.App.4th 1378 (2005)
case_law.holding: §1102.5 'reasonable cause to believe' is objective standard; employee need not prove actual violation, only that reasonable person would believe disclosure revealed violation
case_law.significance: Sets objective standard for protected disclosure — employee does not need to be correct

case_law.citation: Mokler v. County of Orange, 157 Cal.App.4th 121 (2007)
case_law.holding: §1102.5 protects anticipatory disclosure; employer cannot avoid liability by acting before employee makes formal complaint
case_law.significance: Pre-2013 case establishing anticipated disclosure protection — codified in 2013 amendment
